I will introduce a deterministic rule-based fallback mechanism specifically targeting numeric tokens and punctuation-separated variants when the primary frequency-based lookup fails. By parsing out-of-vocabulary strings for integers and decimals and converting them to their canonical Russian spoken forms, the pipeline will correct a major source of exact-match failures. Additionally, stripping trailing punctuation marks before querying the lookup dictionary bridges typographical formatting gaps between training and test distributions. This atomic enhancement directly attacks the dense cluster of digit-heavy and punctuation-adjacent tokens that dominate the residual error rate, promising a measurable boost in sequence accuracy without altering the core training logic.

print("Loading data...")

# Ensure string types
for df in [train_df, test_df]:

        df[col] = df[col].astype(str)

# --- Hold-out Validation Split (90/10) ---
rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
indices = rng.permutation(len(train_df))
split_idx = int(len(train_df) * 0.9)
train_split = train_df.iloc[indices[:split_idx]].reset_index(drop=True)
val_split = train_df.iloc[indices[split_idx:]].reset_index(drop=True)

print(f"Training size: {len(train_split)}, Validation size: {len(val_split)}")

# --- Build Lookup Table from Training Split Only ---
def get_mode_group(series):
    return series.value_counts().index[0]

lookup_dict = train_split.groupby("before")["after"].agg(get_mode_group).to_dict()
print(f"Lookup table built with {len(lookup_dict)} unique mappings.")
